Goals: - Every session readable and drivable from the laptop Nest.
- Several sessions on screen at once, like tmux panes.
- New sessions start inside Nest, with no desktop window.
- Missions and Inbox use the laptop width.
Key product decisions: - Use structured input as the source of truth for generated docs.
- Keep generated write paths local and repo-bounded.
Overview: Nest is built for the Fold first. On the laptop the owner still runs sessions in terminals because the laptop Desk lacks the chat, cannot show several sessions at once and cannot start a session that stays inside Nest. This pass brings the laptop layout to the point where terminals become optional.

Goals: - The owner steers work and personal projects from nest or deck. Terminal sessions are kept for deep repo work.
- Most missions finish with only an FYI. The rest stop at one clear question with buttons.
- Every live run reads as one plain sentence. Raw trails are available but never pushed.
- Every model source is used for what it does best. Work data never leaves Claude accounts; private personal data never leaves the owner's machines.
- Every repeat costs less than the last: failures, manual gestures and corrections feed a weekly pass.
- It is fun to use and fun to tinker with.
Overview: crow today is a hub you drive from terminal sessions: skills, `crow dispatch` and `crow runs`, the deck TUI (MR pane, agents panel), review ledgers, Logics, cdx accounts. The Jarvis layer turns it into an assistant you steer from one interface. You state a goal; a mission runs it in the background through cdx; you only see questions, approvals, proposals and short status. Detail stays one tap away: the MR pane, the live terminal, the full trail.
- **The owner's wishes**, collected in five question rounds on 2026-11-06.

- **Ultron**, a colleague's cockpit: Claude Code background sessions on one Mac around a two-gate workflow (plan, then report). About two weeks old, React PWA, iPhone. Private copy: `local/reference/ultron-design.md`.

- **Jarvis**, a colleague's operations assistant: missions that come back merged and deployed, a vanilla-JS PWA (HQ), a chat gateway, three hosts on a tailnet, nightly self-repair, home and personal pages. Private copy: `local/reference/jarvis-design-document.md`.
Both colleagues already use cdx and Logics, so most of their ideas port with little friction.

core is one always-on service. It owns missions, the inbox, the scheduler, the router and policy. Runs talk to it through files in a mission dir. Every surface reads one HTTP API. core alone publishes.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: On the laptop the Desk shows the selected session or run as the item_177 chat (full message text, tool folds, Earlier, send, permission answers, Pause and Stop), checked against an approved laptop board.
- AC2: The owner types into any live session and answers its prompts from the laptop, and the reply shows in the chat without a page reload.
- AC3: Two or more session chats are visible side by side on the laptop, the owner picks which sessions fill the panes, and keyboard keys move focus and send.

- AC4: The owner starts a new interactive session in a registered project from Nest; it runs without opening a window on the desktop, appears in Nest, and its chat works at once. Opening the same session in a terminal stays possible.
- AC5: Missions on the laptop matches the approved missions-board boards on live data.
- AC6: Inbox on the laptop has its own layout, from a board the owner approved before the build.

- See several sessions at once, side by side like tmux panes.

- Laptop layouts for Missions and Inbox, which today fall back to the Fold inner layouts.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: From Nest on the phone the owner asks the butler to start, steer or check work, and the butler acts through core actions only, with the same confirmations and approvals as a tap.
- AC2: The owner reads and writes inside any running mission or session from Nest, and the phone gets a push when one needs them.
- AC3: The owner reads flagged mail and today's meetings, approves a drafted reply, and accepts or declines a meeting from Nest. Nothing is sent without an approval on the exact text.
- AC4: brief, daily, eod, wrap, weekly and retro start from Nest as missions and their output reads in Nest.
- AC5: Nest and core answer while the laptop sleeps, or the gap is a decided, written limit.
- AC6: A retro is a mission; each proposed crow fix is an inbox item; an approved fix runs as a build mission on cr-0w.
Needs: - Owner, 2026-11-10: "nearly not have to open a terminal anymore and just talk in nest to the orchestrator butler chat or in missions/sessions/runs themselves, handle my calendar, mails". Also: run retros on crow easily, maybe as missions.
- Owner, 2026-11-10: "basically most runs will be missions". Missions are the main run path. Plain sessions and `crow dispatch` stay reachable but come second in every list and action.
- The owner picked all four gap groups (2026-11-10): butler chat; session and mission chat plus push; mail and calendar; rituals plus always-on core. Retros: retro mission kind.
